# Agent Admin API — Agent Resources

Per-agent resource endpoints for the [Agent Admin API](./agent-api.md): the allowed-tools list, API tokens, plugins, chat token usage, repos, chat credentials, agent ask, the platform OpenAPI document, and the GitHub installations snapshot. See [`docs/agent-api.md`](./agent-api.md) for core agent CRUD, authentication, environment variables, and runtime config, and [`docs/agent-api-ops.md`](./agent-api-ops.md) for cron jobs and cron runs.

Base path: `/agents` (same resource as the core API — these are additional routes under it).

---

## Tools (allowed-tools list)

The allowed-tools list controls which Claude Code tools the agent can call.

### Add tool

```
POST /agents/:id/tools
```

Body: `{ pattern: string }`. Pattern is a glob or exact tool name (e.g. `"Read"`, `"Bash"`, `"mcp__*"`). The tool is created enabled. Returns `201`.

### List tools

```
GET /agents/:id/tools
```

Returns `{ tools: AgentTool[] }` where each entry has `id`, `pattern`, and `enabled`.

### Update tool

```
PATCH /agents/:id/tools/:toolId
```

Body: `{ enabled: boolean }` (required). Returns the updated tool.

### Delete tool

```
DELETE /agents/:id/tools/:toolId
```

Returns `204`.

---

## API tokens

Per-agent bearer tokens for scoped API access. The raw token is returned once at creation; only its SHA-256 hash is stored.

### Create token

```
POST /agents/:id/tokens
```

Body (optional): `{ label?: string }`. Returns `201` with `{ token: { id, agentId, label, createdAt, revokedAt }, rawToken }` where `rawToken` is the raw value — save it immediately.

### List tokens

```
GET /agents/:id/tokens
```

Returns `{ tokens: AgentToken[] }` (metadata only — the hash is never returned). Raw token values are never returned after creation.

### Revoke token

```
DELETE /agents/:id/tokens/:tokenId
```

Soft-deletes the token (sets `revokedAt`). Returns `204`.

---

## Plugins

Plugins are Claude Code marketplace plugins installed for the agent.

### Install plugin

```
POST /agents/:id/plugins
```

Body: `{ name: string, version?: string | null }`. The plugin is installed enabled. Returns `201`.

### List plugins

```
GET /agents/:id/plugins
```

Returns `{ plugins: AgentPlugin[] }`.

### Update plugin

```
PATCH /agents/:id/plugins
```

Query param: `name` (required). Body: `{ version?: string | null }`. Returns the updated plugin.

### Remove plugin

```
DELETE /agents/:id/plugins
```

Query param: `name` (required). Returns `204`.

---

## Chat token usage

Daily aggregate of Slack chat session token usage.

### Record daily usage

```
POST /agents/:id/chat-tokens/daily
```

Atomic upsert — accumulates usage into the existing rows for `(agentId, date, model)` tuples if they exist. When a single day spans multiple models (e.g., agent tools using different Claude versions), supply a `modelBreakdown` array to split usage by model.

Body:

| Field | Required | Description |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| `date` | yes | `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `modelBreakdown` | yes | Array of per-model usage entries. Each entry: `{ model: string, inputTokens: number, outputTokens: number, cacheReadTokens: number, cacheCreationTokens: number, costUsd: number }` |

Returns an array of updated daily rows (one per model in the breakdown).

### Chat token stats

```
GET /agents/chat-tokens/daily/stats
```

Self-serve variant: `GET /agents/{id}/chat-tokens/daily/stats` returns the same shape scoped to one agent, with no admin scope required (agent's own token, admin, or member session).

Admin-only. Aggregated chat-token daily stats across all agents broken down by model. Query params: `from` and `to` (optional `YYYY-MM-DD` date strings).

Returns `{ totals, byAgent, byModel, daily }` where each aggregate includes `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, `cacheCreationTokens`, and `costUsd`.

## GitHub installations snapshot

One row per agent, holding the agent's most recently reported GitHub App installations. Replace-all: each `PUT` overwrites the stored list wholesale, so an installation absent from the latest body is dropped. The row is deleted when the agent is deleted. Auth: an admin key/session, or the agent's own bearer token (a token owned by a different agent gets `403`).

### Put snapshot

```
PUT /agents/:id/github-installations
```

Body (closed schema — any unknown field, such as a token, is rejected with `400`):

| Field | Required | Description |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| `reportedAt` | yes | ISO timestamp when the agent reported this list |
| `installations` | yes | Array of `{ owner: string, installationId: positive integer, state: string (max 50), lastError?: string \| null (max 500, sanitized) }`; each entry is also closed |
| `repos` | no | Per-repo access probe result: array of `{ repo: string, owner: string, read: boolean, write: boolean, checkedAt: ISO timestamp, error?: "not_found" \| "forbidden" \| "rate_limited" \| "network" }`; each entry is closed. Omitting it leaves the stored result unchanged; `[]` clears it |

`repos` is sent only by a runtime whose config bundle has `features.repoAccessCheck` true (admin `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_REPO_ACCESS_CHECK_ENABLED=enabled`). The runtime does `GET https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}` for each scoped repo with the owner's installation token (or the `GH_TOKEN` PAT when no healthy installation matches) and maps `permissions.pull` to `read` and `permissions.push` to `write`; `repo` is the bare repo name. It probes at most once per 30-minute installations heartbeat, and again when the repo scope changes, three repos at a time. The token is never logged or stored. On failure `read` and `write` are both `false` and `error` says why:

| `error` | Meaning |
|---------|---------|
| `not_found` | `404`: the repo does not exist, or the credential cannot see it |
| `forbidden` | `403`/`401`, or no credential exists for the owner |
| `rate_limited` | `429`, or a `403` with `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0` |
| `network` | the request failed, timed out, or GitHub answered `5xx` |

Returns `200` with:

```json
{
  "snapshot": {
    "id": "string",
    "agentId": "string",
    "reportedAt": "ISO timestamp",
    "installations": [{ "owner": "string", "installationId": 123, "state": "string", "lastError": "string (optional)" }],
    "repoAccess": [{ "repo": "string", "owner": "string", "read": true, "write": false, "checkedAt": "ISO timestamp", "error": "string (optional)" }],
    "createdAt": "ISO timestamp"
  }
}
```

### Get snapshot

```
GET /agents/:id/github-installations
```

Returns `200` with the latest snapshot in the same `{ snapshot: { ... } }` format, or `404` if the agent has never reported one.

## Tokens, chat credentials and chat-token usage

Three similarly named resources, three different things:

| Route | What it is | Who may call |
|---|---|---|
| `/agents/{id}/tokens` | Admin-API bearer tokens for the agent (`swt_v1_...`). Raw value returned once on create; only a hash is stored. | Per the generic agent-route auth. |
| `/agents/{id}/chat-credentials` | Chat-service tokens scoped to the agent, minted and revoked through admin. | `*` and `platform.ops` only — never the agent's own key. |
| `/agents/{id}/chat-tokens/daily` | Daily LLM token **usage** rollups (counts per model). Not a credential. | Per the generic agent-route auth. |

### Chat credentials

- `POST /agents/{id}/chat-credentials` with `{label}` → `201 {tokenId, rawToken, label, agentId}`.
  The raw token is returned once; admin never stores or logs it. The body is
  closed: an `agentId` field is a 400, so the token is always scoped to `{id}`
  and an unrestricted chat admin token cannot be minted here.
- `GET /agents/{id}/chat-credentials` → `{credentials: [{tokenId, label, agentId}]}` (no raw values).
- `DELETE /agents/{id}/chat-credentials/{tokenId}` → `204`. A token not scoped
  to `{id}` is a 404 and is not revoked.

Each mint and revoke writes one structured log line
`{event: "chat-credential.mint" | "chat-credential.revoke", agentId, tokenId, label, callerLabel}`.

**Required scope:** `*` or `platform.ops`. **Flag:** the routes are off by default: they return 404 unless
`SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_TOKEN_MINT_ENABLED=enabled`. They return 503 when the chat
service client is not configured (`SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_SERVICE_URL` and
`SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_SERVICE_ADMIN_TOKEN`).

## Agent ask

One agent asks another a question through admin. The question lands as the
user message of a new chat thread on the target agent (`kind: "ask"`,
`askFromAgentId`, `askDepth: 1`, title `ask from <from> - <ISO time>`).

- `POST /agents/{id}/ask` with `{from, question, waitMs?, depth?, ttlSeconds?}` →
  `201 {askId, threadId, status, reply?}`.
  - `question`: 1-8000 chars. `waitMs`: 0-60000, default 0. `ttlSeconds`:
    60-3600, default 600. `depth`: only 1 is accepted (`400 {error: "depth is capped at 1"}`).
  - `waitMs > 0` polls the thread once per second until the agent replies
    (`status: "replied"` with `reply`) or the budget ends (`status: "pending"`).
    `waitMs: 0` returns `pending` right away.
  - Callers: `*`, `platform.ops`, or the agent key whose id equals `from`.
    An agent key may call another agent's `/ask` path, but only as itself;
    any other `from` is a 403.
  - The `from>{id}` pair must be on `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_ASK_ALLOWLIST`, else
    `403 {error: "ask not allowed for this pair"}` and nothing reaches the chat service.
- `GET /agents/{id}/asks?limit&offset` → `{asks, total, limit, offset}`: the
  AgentAsk audit rows the agent sent or received, newest first. `*`,
  `platform.read` and `platform.ops` only.

Every ask writes an AgentAsk audit row (`fromAgentId`, `toAgentId`, `threadId`,
`depth`, `waitMs`, `ttlSeconds`, `status`, `callerLabel`, `createdAt`,
`repliedAt`) before the chat call and updates it after (`status` ends as
`pending`, `replied` or `failed`). The question text is never stored. Each ask
also logs one structured line `{event: "agent-ask", askId, from, to, status, callerLabel}`
(never the question).

The routes return `404 {error: "Not found"}` unless
`SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_ASK_ENABLED=enabled`, and the ask route returns
`503 {error: "chat service not configured"}` when `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_SERVICE_URL`
and `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_SERVICE_ADMIN_TOKEN` are not both set.

## Transcripts

Redacted cron-run session transcripts, uploaded by the runtime and read back
by admin callers.

- `PUT /agents/{id}/crons/{cronId}/runs/{runId}/transcript` with
  `{sessionId?, body, truncated, redactions}` → `200 {runId, bytes, truncated, redactions}`.
  Callers: the agent's own key, or `*`. The run must belong to the cron and the
  agent (same rule as the cron-run `PATCH`), else 404. `body` over 1 MiB
  (UTF-8 bytes) is a 413. The row is upserted by `runId`, then the agent is
  swept down to its newest 200 transcripts.
- `GET` on the same path → `{runId, cronId, sessionId, bytes, truncated, redactions, createdAt, body}`.
  `*`, `platform.read` and `platform.ops` only. An agent key is 403 even for
  its own runs. An `AgentTranscriptRead` row (`runId`, `agentId`, `reader`,
  `scopeKind`, `at`) is written before the response; if that write fails the
  body is not served. 404 when absent.

**Posture.** Transcripts are admin-only, and the whole surface is flagged off:
both routes return `404` unless `SHIPWRIGHT_TRANSCRIPT_API_ENABLED=enabled`.
The body is capped at 1 MiB and never appears in logs. Every read is audited.
Redaction happens on the runtime before upload (live `SECRET_ENV_VARS` values
plus token shapes such as `ghp_`, `github_pat_`, `sk-ant-`, `xox*-`, `AKIA`,
PEM private keys, bearer tokens and JWTs); admin stores what it is sent. The
runtime uploads only when the config bundle's `features.transcriptUpload` is
true (the same flag), reads `$AGENT_HOME/dot-claude/projects/<encoded cwd>/<sessionId>.jsonl`,
tail-truncates to 1 MiB on whole lines with a marker line first, and never
fails a run over an upload problem.

## Repos (add and remove)

`PATCH /agents/{id}` replaces the whole `repos` array. These two routes change it incrementally:

- `POST /agents/{id}/repos` with `{repos: ["org/repo", ...]}` unions the entries into the agent's list, keeping existing order and appending new ones. Idempotent: adding a repo the agent already has is a no-op. Returns the full updated agent.
- `DELETE /agents/{id}/repos/{owner}/{name}` removes one `owner/name` repo, keeping the order of the rest. `404` when the agent does not have it. Returns the full updated agent.

A resulting list with two repos that share a basename is a `400` (the agent's `repos/<name>` clone folders are keyed by basename).

**Required scope:** `*`, the agent's own key, or `platform.ops` (both routes are on `PLATFORM_OPS_ROUTES`; `platform.read` is 403). **Flag:** none, always mounted.

## Platform OpenAPI document (`/doc`)

`GET /doc` returns the platform OpenAPI 3.1 document (admin CRUD plus runtime routes, never extension paths), `Content-Type: application/json`, `Cache-Control: no-store`. The body is byte-identical to the committed `admin/openapi.platform.json`.

**Required scope:** any credential the admin auth middleware accepts (bearer key or session cookie). **Flag:** `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_DOC_ENABLED=enabled`; when unset the route is not mounted and returns `404`.
